title.narrative: Supporting Engaged Responses for Vulnerable communities in Emergencies (SERVE)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe SERVE project targets a total of 69,250 individuals (15,254 girls, 19,146 women, 15,744 boys, and 19,106 men) through multi-sectorial interventions designed to support and strengthen the delivery of critical basic services through build resiliency for the most vulnerable people against the impact of the socio-economic crisis. Three sectors were prioritized based on the needs identified in assessments of the potential locations education, WASH, and food security. All planned interventions overlap in the same geographic areas, either within in the project or complementary activities implemented by ADRA / other organizations and thus the total number of beneficiaries under each sector do not equal the total number of beneficiaries. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtWASH interventions will result in approximately 67,000 vulnerable individuals having access to greater amounts of water, thus reducing the need for water trucking and saving money. This will be achieved through a variety of interventions (including network, high tank, and borehole rehabilitation, as well as the provision of solar system and connecting boreholes to exempted of ration electricity lines) based on the individual assessed needs of each community. Beneficiaries were calculated from population estimates from local sources. ltbrgtEducation activities will ensure the protection of 990 vulnerable children (including 250 girls and 740 boys) and 60 of their teachers, against socio-economic conditions through school rehabilitation (provision of doors, windows, heaters, and rehabilitation of disability-accessible and segregated WASH facilities) and NFE to enable the return to and retention in formal education. Beneficiaries were calculated through existing and anticipated children in the schools. The number of boys is higher than girls as 1 of the 2 targeted schools are nonfunctional boys’ schools. However, a larger number of girls will indirectly benefit as the opening of the boys’ primary school in Maliha will enable the functional high school (including secondary and lower secondary students) to be segregated and the lower secondary children to be on their mixed school that host the primary children now. The interventions will also reduce the current number of children per classroom in existing schools.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbrgt ltbrgt ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtFSA sector – In Nawa, Daraa, rehabilitation of one sub-canal out of 6 sub-irrigation canals (C1) benefitting 1,200 individuals (male and female farmers and their households), which will complement previous rehabilitation of the main canal and three out of six sub-canals in Nawa. The planned irrigation canal rehabilitation will improve the production of essential crops such as wheat and vegetables (improving the value chain for vulnerable young children, children, adolescents, young adults, middle-aged adults and older adults as well as PWDs and the elderly) contributing to building their resilience. The length of the rehabilitated sub canal will be 2,500 meters allowing beneficiaries to increase their corps yields.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtProposed interventions complement other previous or planned interventions in the targeted areas to present a holistic approach to programming. ADRA has previous experience in all planned interventions and has been present in the targeted locations since 2015. All proposed activities have been extensively coordinated with the relevant sectors, bi-laterally with other INGOs and relevant ministries to ensure a facilitated approval processes. Protection has been mainstreamed into all project activities and localization of the project has been improved through informal coordination with a local NGO, as well as strengthened community consultations, engagement and formation of local committees. ltbrgtlt/pgt
